The Narration of Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) Concerning the Excessive Istighfaar of Rasulullaah ﷺ
Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, "I have never seen anyone after Rasulullaah ﷺ who more excessively recited:
'I Seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent to Him.'" [^2]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Teaches A Du'aa of Istighfaar to a Man who had Committed many Sins

Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) narrates that a man once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "Alas! How many are my sins! Alas! How many are my sins!" When he repeated himself twice or thrice, Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed him saying, "You should rather say:

"O Allaah! Your forgiveness is greater than my sins and I have more hope in Your mercy than I have in my deeds."
When the man recited the du'aa, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him to repeat it. After he had repeated it once, Rasulullaah ﷺ bade him to repeat it yet again. After repeating it once more, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "You may now leave because Allaah has forgiven all your sins." [^3]

blocks.text: Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) Encourage people to Engage in Istighfaar

Hadhrat Hannaad narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) overheard someone saying, "(اَسْتَغْفِرُ اللّٰهَ وَاَتُوْبُ اِلَيْهِ) ('I seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent to Him')", Hadhrat Umar (RA) addressed him saying, "Is that All? Why do you not follow it up with its partner: (فَاغْفِرْ لِيْ وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ) ('So do forgive me and accept my repentance')." [^4]

Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I am surprised at the person who destroys himself when salvation is at hand." "What is the salvation?" someone asked. "It is Istighfaar," came the reply. [^5]
Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Glad tidings for the person who finds in his record of deeds even a little bit of Istighfaar." [^6]
